description: Product-supported FFmpeg capabilities (PRD FR-3). Source of truth for what fass may build. Actual encoder/filter availability depends on the installed FFmpeg build — check with `fass env` or `--preflight`.

tested_ffmpeg.notes: libx264, libhevc, libvpx-vp9, aac, libopus verified present on the development machine

h264.requires: libx264 — present in nearly all builds

h265.requires: libhevc — built into FFmpeg, but encoding is slower
h265.note: Smaller files than H.264 at similar quality; slower to encode.

flv.stream_only_note: H.264+AAC only — what RTMP/RTMPS endpoints carry

rtsp.stream_only_note: output only to an rtsp(s):// destination; never a file

srt.stream_only_note: output only to an srt:// destination; never a file

streaming.description: Stream / remote I/O (M3b). Inputs may be URLs with an allowlisted scheme (they are read by the user's local ffmpeg — fass never fetches or executes); outputs may be stream destinations, whose scheme fixes the container. Everything stays an argv token; stream destinations are disclosed in the explanation.
streaming.note: HTTP output (e.g. HLS .m3u8) is not in the MVP stream set — it writes segment files locally and needs per-destination tuning. Scheme defaults come from https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-formats.html (rtmp->flv, rtsp->rtsp, udp/rtp/tcp->mpegts); fass still emits an explicit -f for stream destinations.

bitrate_policy: An explicit target video bitrate (plan.output.video_bitrate_kbps) overrides the quality preset: -b:v and -maxrate at the target, plus -bufsize at 2x the target for H.264/H.265 (a CBR-style target; audio keeps its codec-preset bitrate).

pixel_formats.description: Output pixel formats per video codec (the scaling/pixel-format-conversion component). The codec's video_codecs[*].pix_fmt is the default; yuv420p10le is the 10-bit form, yuv444p full chroma (VP9 only in the MVP).

video_profiles.description: Encoder profiles (H.264 in the MVP): 'baseline' maximizes compatibility with old players.

video_presets.description: x264 speed/quality trade-off presets (H.264 in the MVP; libhevc/libvpx-vp9 presets differ and are not exposed).

audio_resample.description: Audio resampler targets: -ar sample rate (Hz) and -ac channel count (1 mono, 2 stereo, 6 5.1).

speed.description: Playback-speed change: setpts=PTS/factor on video, an atempo chain on audio (atempo accepts 0.5-2.0 per instance, so larger factors chain instances).

crop.description: Crop to exact output dimensions, centered (FFmpeg's crop default).

bitstream_filters.description: Stream-copy (remux) bitstream filters. When remuxing from an MP4/MOV container to MPEG-TS, H.264/HEVC must be restamped into Annex-B form; when remuxing AAC audio out of MPEG-TS into MP4/MOV, the ADTS header must be stripped. Filters run on the compressed stream only, without re-encoding.

sources.description: Generic ffmpeg input sources (the input/output-devices component). An asset whose path is '<format>:<spec>' with an allowlisted format is a source spec, not a file: it gets -f <format> plus ;key=value options as separate option tokens. Output devices carry audio only (pcm) — a plan that produces video cannot target one.

resize.description: Scale the video. A height (e.g. 720p) or width keeps the aspect ratio; width+height letterboxes (preserve) or stretches (exact).
resize.note: A 720p request sets the output height to 720 with an aspect-compatible even width — it does not pad or crop to 1280x720.

grayscale.description: Remove color from the video (black and white). Audio is unaffected.

watermark.description: Overlay one static image throughout the output.
watermark.note: Image is shown at original size unless scaled; margin is in output pixels; the overlay persists for the whole interval (single-frame input never bounds duration).

audio_replace.description: Replace the output audio with the first audio stream of another input (an audio file).
audio_replace.note: Emits -map N:a:0 for the replacement input plus -shortest, so the output ends when the shorter of the video and the replacement audio ends. The replacement audio is encoded to the container's audio codec (no stream copy).

crop.description: Crop to exact output dimensions, centered (FFmpeg's crop default).
crop.note: Width/height snap to even (yuv420p); the planner rejects a crop larger than the probed source dimensions.

speed.audio: -af atempo chain (0.5-2.0 per instance, chained for larger factors)
speed.note: A trim's source duration is divided by the factor; the output is shorter than the cut interval.

rotate.description: Rotate by a quarter turn (90/180/270; clockwise by default).
rotate.filter: transpose=1 (90 CW), transpose=2 (90 CCW / 270 CW), hflip+vflip (180)

audio_resample.description: Resample the audio to a target sample rate and/or channel count.
audio_resample.note: Targets come from the audio_resample matrix; an audio-removed plan cannot resample.

subtitles.description: Add subtitles from a bound subtitle file (srt/ass/ssa/vtt), burned in (default) or as a selectable track.
subtitles.filter: subtitles= (srt/vtt) / ass= (ass/ssa) for burn; -map N:s:0 + -c:s for soft
subtitles.note: See the top-level 'subtitles' block: burn forces a re-encode, soft muxes mov_text (mp4/mov) or srt (mkv) and is copy-compatible. At most one subtitle operation per plan; the subtitle asset is bound outside the model.

subtitles.description: Subtitle support (the subtitles/demuxer-encoder component). Subtitles arrive as a typed asset (srt/ass/ssa/vtt) and are either burned into the video (hard-coded, libass) or muxed as a selectable track (soft).
subtitles.note: burn uses the libass filters 'subtitles=' (srt/vtt) or 'ass=' (ass/ssa) in the video filter chain and forces a video re-encode; the filename needs two layers of FFmpeg filter escaping (graph parser, then filter-option parser). soft muxes a selectable track: mp4/mov → mov_text, mkv → srt (encoded from the source format); other containers (webm, mpegts, flv, rtsp, srt) have no soft-subtitle codec and soft mode is rejected there. soft mode never forces a video re-encode — it is compatible with -c copy. Filenames containing ':' cannot be handled by FFmpeg at all (its URL layer parses them as a protocol); the planner rejects them with a clear error. No -shortest: subtitles may legitimately be shorter or longer than the video.

stream_selection.audio: 0:a:0 (first audio stream only; additional streams are excluded). With audio_replace, the mapped audio stream is the first audio stream of the replacement input instead.
stream_selection.note: Additional streams beyond the first video and first audio are not carried over (visible notice in the explanation). Subtitle streams are the exception only when a soft-subtitle operation is present, in which case the first subtitle stream of the subtitle asset is mapped.

trim_policy: Trimming re-encodes: the MVP prioritizes accurate cuts over fast stream-copy cuts (PRD FR-4).
copy_policy: Stream copy (remux) is chosen only when no filters are required AND media metadata proves the input streams already match the requested codecs. Without metadata the planner re-encodes and says so. Soft subtitles are compatible with copy (mapped with -map N:s:0 and encoded with -c:s, overriding -c copy for that stream only); burning subtitles is a filter and forces a re-encode.

docs_provenance.devices: https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-devices.html (lavfi, v4l2, alsa, dshow, avfoundation, x11grab)
